_note: Company profiles for the About pill on the valuation cards. Facts from Financial Modeling Prep company profiles; 'about' is a plain-English summary. capAsOf is the day the market value was read (used only for the size class).

FIS.name: Fidelity National Information Services
FIS.about: FIS runs the technology behind banks: the core systems that keep accounts, online and mobile banking, fraud checks, and the networks that move money between them. Its capital markets arm sells trading, lending and treasury software to investment firms.

DOX.name: Amdocs
DOX.about: Amdocs builds and runs the billing, customer care and network software that phone, cable and media companies use to sell and charge for their services. Much of its revenue comes from long-term managed-services contracts with large telecom carriers.

MKC.name: McCormick & Company
MKC.about: McCormick is the world's largest spice and seasoning maker, behind brands like McCormick, French's, Frank's RedHot, Cholula and Old Bay. A second arm, Flavor Solutions, sells custom seasonings and flavors to food manufacturers and restaurant chains.

MZTI.name: The Marzetti Company
MZTI.about: Marzetti (formerly Lancaster Colony) makes salad dressings, dips, croutons, frozen garlic bread and dinner rolls, under its own brands and licensed restaurant names. It sells to grocery stores and to restaurant chains across the U.S.

NKE.name: Nike
NKE.about: Nike is the world's largest athletic footwear and apparel company, with the Nike, Jordan and Converse brands. It sells through its own stores and website as well as sporting goods and department stores worldwide.

GIS.name: General Mills
GIS.about: General Mills makes cereals, snacks, baking mixes, soups and frozen foods under brands like Cheerios, Nature Valley, Pillsbury, Betty Crocker and Häagen-Dazs. It also owns Blue Buffalo, a fast-growing pet food business.

PGR.name: Progressive
PGR.about: Progressive is one of the largest U.S. car insurers, selling personal and commercial auto policies directly online and through independent agents. It also insures homes, motorcycles, boats and RVs. Unusually, it pays most of its dividend as one large annual payment.

INTU.name: Intuit
INTU.about: Intuit makes TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp — software for filing taxes, running small-business books, tracking personal credit and email marketing. Most of its revenue comes from subscriptions.

TSCO.name: Tractor Supply
TSCO.about: Tractor Supply is the largest U.S. farm and ranch retailer, with over 2,000 stores selling animal feed, pet supplies, fencing, tools and workwear to hobby farmers and rural homeowners. It also runs the Petsense pet store chain.

CMCSA.name: Comcast
CMCSA.about: Comcast sells internet, TV and mobile service under the Xfinity brand and owns NBCUniversal — NBC, Telemundo, Peacock, Universal film studios and the Universal theme parks. It also owns Sky, a major European pay-TV provider.

BAH.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
BAH.about: Booz Allen is a consulting and technology firm that works mainly for the U.S. government, especially defense and intelligence agencies. Its work covers cybersecurity, data analytics, AI and engineering of complex systems.

WLK.name: Westlake
WLK.about: Westlake makes basic plastics and chemicals — polyethylene, PVC and chlor-alkali — and turns part of that output into building products like vinyl siding, trim, roofing, windows and PVC pipe. Its earnings swing with the chemical cycle and with housing construction.

AMSF.name: AMERISAFE
AMSF.about: AMERISAFE sells workers' compensation insurance to small and mid-sized businesses in high-risk trades such as construction, trucking, logging and agriculture. It pays a modest regular dividend and has often added large special dividends from excess capital.

PAYX.name: Paychex
PAYX.about: Paychex runs payroll, HR, benefits and retirement plans for small and mid-sized businesses, mostly in the U.S. It also earns interest on the client payroll funds it holds before paying them out.

KMB.name: Kimberly-Clark
KMB.about: Kimberly-Clark makes everyday paper and personal care products: Huggies and Pull-Ups diapers, Kleenex tissues, Scott and Cottonelle bath tissue, Kotex and Depend. It sells in grocery and big-box stores worldwide and to offices and hotels.

ACN.name: Accenture
ACN.about: Accenture is the world's largest IT consulting and outsourcing firm, helping large companies and governments with strategy, cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity and back-office operations. It is incorporated in Ireland.

CLX.name: Clorox
CLX.about: Clorox makes bleach and cleaning products plus a set of household brands: Glad bags, Kingsford charcoal, Fresh Step cat litter, Hidden Valley dressing, Brita water filters and Burt's Bees. Most of its sales are in the U.S.

CAPMF.name: Capgemini
CAPMF.about: Capgemini is a French IT consulting, engineering and outsourcing firm, one of Europe's largest, serving banks, manufacturers, retailers and governments worldwide. Its main listing is in Paris; in the U.S. it trades over the counter.

BR.name: Broadridge Financial Solutions
BR.about: Broadridge handles the plumbing of investing: it distributes proxy votes and shareholder mailings for most U.S. public companies and funds, and runs trade processing and settlement systems for banks and brokers. Much of its revenue is recurring.

OTEX.name: Open Text
OTEX.about: OpenText makes software that helps large organizations store, manage and secure their documents and data, plus cybersecurity products such as Webroot and Carbonite. It is based in Canada and grew largely through acquisitions.

HRL.name: Hormel Foods
HRL.about: Hormel makes packaged meats and snacks under brands like SPAM, Skippy, Planters, Jennie-O turkey, Applegate and Hormel bacon. It sells to grocery stores, restaurants and delis in the U.S. and abroad.

PEP.name: PepsiCo
PEP.about: PepsiCo sells drinks and snacks worldwide: Pepsi, Gatorade and Mountain Dew on the beverage side, and Frito-Lay chips (Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos) plus Quaker oats on the food side. Snacks bring in the larger share of profit.

PRGO.name: Perrigo
PRGO.about: Perrigo is the leading maker of store-brand over-the-counter medicines — the pharmacy's own label of allergy, cough, pain and digestive remedies — plus infant formula and some branded products like Mederma and Compeed. It is incorporated in Ireland.

UVV.name: Universal Corporation
UVV.about: Universal is the world's largest leaf tobacco merchant: it buys, processes and ships raw tobacco to cigarette and cigar makers. A newer ingredients arm makes fruit and vegetable ingredients and flavorings for food and pet food companies.

EMN.name: Eastman Chemical
EMN.about: Eastman makes specialty plastics, additives and fibers used in cars, packaging, building materials, personal care and electronics, plus acetate tow for cigarette filters. It was spun off from Eastman Kodak in 1993.

TNC.name: Tennant
TNC.about: Tennant makes commercial floor-cleaning machines — scrubbers, sweepers and robotic cleaners — used in warehouses, stores, airports, schools and hospitals. Parts, consumables and service bring in steady repeat revenue.

MDLZ.name: Mondelez International
MDLZ.about: Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack makers, with Oreo, Ritz and belVita biscuits and Cadbury, Milka and Toblerone chocolate. Most of its sales come from outside North America. It is the former Kraft Foods, renamed in 2012.

MATW.name: Matthews International
MATW.about: Matthews makes bronze and granite memorials, caskets and cremation equipment for funeral homes and cemeteries, plus industrial equipment such as product-marking systems and warehouse automation. It also has a brand-packaging design business.

RHI.name: Robert Half
RHI.about: Robert Half places temporary and full-time staff in accounting, finance, technology and admin roles, and owns Protiviti, a risk and internal-audit consulting firm. Its results rise and fall with hiring demand.

CWT.name: California Water Service Group
CWT.about: California Water Service supplies drinking water to about half a million homes and businesses in 100 California communities, plus smaller systems in Washington, New Mexico, Hawaii and Texas. State regulators set the rates it can charge.

HSY.name: Hershey
HSY.about: Hershey is the largest U.S. chocolate maker — Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat (in the U.S.), Kisses, Jolly Rancher and Twizzlers — and has added salty snacks like SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels. Cocoa prices are a key cost swing.

ARTNA.name: Artesian Resources
ARTNA.about: Artesian is Delaware's largest water utility, serving roughly 95,000 customers in Delaware plus a few thousand in Maryland and Pennsylvania, and it also runs wastewater systems. State regulators set its rates.

CTSH.name: Cognizant Technology Solutions
CTSH.about: Cognizant is a large IT services and outsourcing firm, with most of its workforce in India, that builds and runs software and back-office operations for banks, insurers, healthcare companies and manufacturers.

OWL.name: Blue Owl Capital
OWL.about: Blue Owl is an alternative asset manager focused on private lending to mid-sized companies, buying minority stakes in other private-equity firms, and sale-leaseback real estate. Most of its fees come from long-term or permanent capital, which makes them steady.

LOW.name: Lowe's
LOW.about: Lowe's is the second-largest U.S. home improvement retailer, with about 1,700 stores selling appliances, tools, lumber, paint, flooring and garden supplies to homeowners and contractors. Sales track housing turnover and renovation spending.

EIX.name: Edison International
EIX.about: Edison International owns Southern California Edison, the electric utility serving about 15 million people across Southern, Central and Coastal California. Wildfire liability is the main risk investors watch.

BF-B.name: Brown-Forman
BF-B.about: Brown-Forman makes spirits led by Jack Daniel's whiskey, plus Woodford Reserve and Old Forester bourbons, Herradura and el Jimador tequila, and Finlandia vodka. The founding Brown family still controls the company.

POR.name: Portland General Electric
POR.about: Portland General Electric generates and delivers electricity to about 950,000 homes and businesses in and around Portland, Oregon, from hydro, wind, gas and purchased power. Oregon regulators set its rates.

HD.name: Home Depot
HD.about: Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer, with over 2,300 stores selling building materials, tools, appliances and garden supplies to homeowners and professional contractors. It has expanded its pro business with the purchase of SRS Distribution.

FNF.name: Fidelity National Financial
FNF.about: FNF is the largest U.S. title insurer, protecting buyers and lenders against ownership disputes in home and commercial real estate deals. It also owns most of F&G, a seller of annuities and life insurance. Title revenue swings with home sales and mortgage activity.

INGR.name: Ingredion
INGR.about: Ingredion turns corn, tapioca and other crops into starches, sweeteners and texturizers that food, beverage and brewing companies use to thicken, sweeten and stabilize their products. It was formerly called Corn Products International.

HPQ.name: HP Inc.
HPQ.about: HP makes personal computers and printers, and earns much of its profit from ink and toner supplies. It is the PC and printing half of the original Hewlett-Packard, which split in two in 2015.

SON.name: Sonoco Products
SON.about: Sonoco makes packaging: metal and paper food cans (like snack and baby formula containers), flexible packaging, and industrial paper tubes and cores used to wind textiles, film and paper. It has been reshaping toward consumer packaging through acquisitions.

TRI.name: Thomson Reuters
TRI.about: Thomson Reuters sells research and workflow software to lawyers, accountants and corporate tax and compliance teams — Westlaw is its flagship — and owns the Reuters news agency. Most revenue is subscription-based. The Thomson family's holding company controls it.

SWKS.name: Skyworks Solutions
SWKS.about: Skyworks designs the radio-frequency chips that let smartphones and other devices connect to cellular and Wi-Fi networks. Apple is its largest customer, so iPhone design wins drive much of its results.

AWR.name: American States Water
AWR.about: American States Water supplies water to about 260,000 customers in California and electricity to a small mountain area of San Bernardino County. It also runs water and wastewater systems on U.S. military bases under long-term contracts. It has raised its dividend for over 70 straight years.

GPC.name: Genuine Parts
GPC.about: Genuine Parts distributes replacement parts: NAPA auto parts stores on one side, and Motion Industries' industrial parts (bearings, hoses, power transmission) on the other. It operates across North America, Europe and Australasia.

ES.name: Eversource Energy
ES.about: Eversource delivers electricity and natural gas to over 4 million customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire, and runs regulated water systems. It was formerly Northeast Utilities.

SCL.name: Stepan
SCL.about: Stepan makes surfactants — the cleaning agents in detergents, shampoos and disinfectants — for consumer-product companies, plus polyols used in building insulation foam. The Stepan family still leads the company.

BXSL.name: Blackstone Secured Lending Fund
BXSL.about: BXSL is a business development company managed by Blackstone that makes senior secured loans to mid-sized private U.S. companies. It must pay out most of its income, so nearly all earnings go to the dividend.

SYY.name: Sysco
SYY.about: Sysco is the largest food distributor to restaurants, hospitals, schools and hotels in North America, delivering everything from fresh produce and meat to napkins and kitchen equipment. It also operates in the U.K., France and other countries.

MCD.name: McDonald's
MCD.about: McDonald's runs the world's largest fast-food chain, with over 40,000 restaurants, about 95% of them run by franchisees. It earns most of its profit as a landlord and franchisor, collecting rent and royalties rather than selling burgers itself.

UPBD.name: Upbound Group
UPBD.about: Upbound (formerly Rent-A-Center) leases furniture, appliances, electronics and tires to customers who may not qualify for regular credit, through Rent-A-Center stores and Acima, a lease-to-own checkout option inside other retailers.

HTO.name: H2O America
HTO.about: H2O America (formerly SJW Group) supplies water to about 400,000 connections — around 1.5 million people — in San Jose, California, Connecticut, Maine and the San Antonio–Austin area of Texas. State regulators set its rates.

KR.name: Kroger
KR.about: Kroger is the largest traditional U.S. supermarket chain, with about 2,700 stores under names like Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer, Harris Teeter and King Soopers, plus pharmacies, fuel centers and a large store-brand business.

WES.name: Western Midstream Partners
WES.about: Western Midstream gathers, processes and transports natural gas, crude oil and produced water, mostly in the Permian Basin of Texas and New Mexico and in the Rockies. Occidental Petroleum is its main customer and largest owner. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

SGU.name: Star Group
SGU.about: Star Group delivers home heating oil and propane to about 400,000 customers, mostly in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, and installs and services heating and air-conditioning systems. Its results depend heavily on how cold the winter is. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

TSN.name: Tyson Foods
TSN.about: Tyson is one of the largest U.S. meat companies, processing chicken, beef and pork and selling prepared foods under Tyson, Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm and Ball Park. Results swing with cattle costs and chicken prices.

TROW.name: T. Rowe Price
TROW.about: T. Rowe Price manages stock and bond mutual funds and retirement assets, with a large share of its money in 401(k) and target-date funds. It earns fees as a percentage of assets, so its income moves with the market. It carries no long-term debt.

AES.name: AES Corporation
AES.about: AES owns power plants and electric utilities in the U.S. and Latin America and is one of the biggest builders of wind, solar and battery projects, often under long-term contracts with tech companies and utilities. It is shifting away from coal.

AVA.name: Avista
AVA.about: Avista supplies electricity and natural gas to about 400,000 electric and 380,000 gas customers in eastern Washington, northern Idaho and parts of Oregon, mostly from hydro power, plus a small utility in Juneau, Alaska.

TRN.name: Trinity Industries
TRN.about: Trinity builds freight and tank railcars and leases out a fleet of over 100,000 of them to shippers in agriculture, energy, chemicals and construction. The leasing side brings steady income; the manufacturing side moves with the rail cycle.

NEE.name: NextEra Energy
NEE.about: NextEra owns Florida Power & Light, the largest U.S. electric utility by customers, serving about 12 million Floridians, and NextEra Energy Resources, the world's largest generator of wind and solar power. It was formerly FPL Group.

AMCR.name: Amcor
AMCR.about: Amcor is one of the world's largest packaging makers: flexible films and pouches for food, medical and personal-care products, and plastic bottles for drinks. It merged with Berry Global in 2025. The current company was formed in 2018 from Amcor's tie-up with Bemis.

ADP.name: Automatic Data Processing
ADP.about: ADP is the largest payroll processor in the world, paying roughly one in six U.S. workers, and also sells HR, benefits and retirement-plan software. It earns interest on client payroll funds it holds before paying them out.

NOG.name: Northern Oil and Gas
NOG.about: Northern Oil and Gas owns minority stakes in thousands of oil and gas wells drilled by other operators in the Williston (North Dakota), Permian and Appalachian basins. It runs with a tiny staff and no drilling rigs of its own, so its results track oil and gas prices.

BAM.name: Brookfield Asset Management
BAM.about: Brookfield Asset Management runs one of the world's largest alternative investment businesses — infrastructure, renewable power, real estate, private equity and private credit — for pension funds, insurers and wealthy investors. It earns fees and pays out most of its earnings. It was spun out of Brookfield Corporation in 2022.

ITW.name: Illinois Tool Works
ITW.about: Illinois Tool Works runs seven industrial businesses: car components, commercial kitchen equipment, test and measurement tools, welding gear, adhesives and fluids, construction fasteners, and specialty packaging products. It is known for high margins and decades of dividend raises.

CNA.name: CNA Financial
CNA.about: CNA is a large U.S. commercial insurer covering professional liability, workers' comp, property and specialty risks for businesses of all sizes, sold through independent agents and brokers. Loews Corporation owns about 90% of it. It often pays a special dividend on top of its regular one.

UNH.name: UnitedHealth Group
UNH.about: UnitedHealth is the largest U.S. health insurer (UnitedHealthcare) and owns Optum, which runs doctor groups and clinics, a major pharmacy-benefit manager and healthcare software and data services. Medicare Advantage is a key profit driver.

VZ.name: Verizon Communications
VZ.about: Verizon is one of the three big U.S. wireless carriers and also sells Fios fiber internet and business network services. It was formed from Bell Atlantic and GTE in 2000. Heavy debt from spectrum purchases is the main point investors watch.

BAC.name: Bank of America
BAC.about: Bank of America is the second-largest U.S. bank, with about 3,700 branches and nearly 70 million consumer and small-business clients. It also owns Merrill (wealth management) and runs a large investment bank and trading business. Interest rates drive much of its profit.

BEP.name: Brookfield Renewable Partners
BEP.about: Brookfield Renewable owns hydro, wind, solar and battery plants across the Americas, Europe and Asia, selling most of its power under long-term contracts, increasingly to tech companies. It is managed by Brookfield and is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

BMY.name: Bristol-Myers Squibb
BMY.about: Bristol-Myers Squibb is a large drugmaker focused on cancer, blood disorders, immunology and heart disease. Its biggest sellers include the blood thinner Eliquis and the cancer drug Opdivo, several of which face patent expiries later this decade.

BMI.name: Badger Meter
BMI.about: Badger Meter makes water meters and the cellular reading network and software that let utilities read them remotely, plus flow-measurement instruments for industry. Most sales go to U.S. water utilities replacing older meters.

SBUX.name: Starbucks
SBUX.about: Starbucks runs or licenses about 40,000 coffee shops worldwide, with the U.S. and China its biggest markets, and sells packaged coffee in grocery stores through a partnership with Nestlé. It is in the middle of a turnaround under its CEO.

EOG.name: EOG Resources
EOG.about: EOG is one of the largest U.S. shale oil and gas producers, drilling in the Permian, Eagle Ford, Utica and other basins, and in Trinidad. It carries little debt and pays special dividends on top of its regular one when oil prices are high. It was spun off from Enron in 1999.

RF.name: Regions Financial
RF.about: Regions is a large regional bank with about 1,250 branches across the South, Midwest and Texas, offering consumer and commercial banking and wealth management.

SJM.name: J. M. Smucker
SJM.about: Smucker sells Folgers and Café Bustelo coffee, Jif peanut butter, Smucker's jams and Uncrustables sandwiches, Milk-Bone and Meow Mix pet foods, and Hostess snacks. Coffee is its biggest profit source.

MDT.name: Medtronic
MDT.about: Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device makers: pacemakers and heart valves, surgical tools and robotics, spine and brain therapies, and diabetes pumps. It is legally based in Ireland, with operational headquarters in Minneapolis.

BIP.name: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners
BIP.about: Brookfield Infrastructure owns toll roads, railroads, ports, gas pipelines, power lines, cell towers and data centers around the world, most earning regulated or contracted fees. It is managed by Brookfield and is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

OGS.name: ONE Gas
OGS.about: ONE Gas delivers natural gas to about 2.3 million homes and businesses through Oklahoma Natural Gas, Kansas Gas Service and Texas Gas Service. It was spun off from ONEOK in 2014, and state regulators set its rates.

ARCC.name: Ares Capital
ARCC.about: Ares Capital is the largest publicly traded business development company, lending to mid-sized private U.S. companies — mostly senior secured loans — and is managed by Ares Management. It must pay out most of its taxable income as dividends.

CTBI.name: Community Trust Bancorp
CTBI.about: Community Trust is a community bank with about 80 branches in eastern and central Kentucky, southern West Virginia and northeastern Tennessee, offering consumer and business loans, deposits and trust services.

GS.name: Goldman Sachs
GS.about: Goldman Sachs is a leading global investment bank: it advises on mergers, underwrites stock and bond offerings, trades securities for big clients, and manages money for institutions and wealthy individuals. Its profits swing with deal-making and market activity.

SBSI.name: Southside Bancshares
SBSI.about: Southside is a community bank based in Tyler, Texas, with branches across East Texas and the Dallas–Fort Worth and Austin areas, offering consumer, commercial and municipal loans and wealth management.

SNA.name: Snap-on
SNA.about: Snap-on makes professional tools, tool storage and diagnostic equipment for auto mechanics and industrial technicians, sold largely from franchisee-driven vans that visit repair shops. It also finances those purchases for mechanics and franchisees.

CBU.name: Community Bank System
CBU.about: Community Bank System runs about 200 branches across upstate New York, Pennsylvania, Vermont and Massachusetts, and has sizable fee businesses in employee benefits administration, insurance and wealth management.

YUM.name: Yum! Brands
YUM.about: Yum! Brands franchises KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, with over 60,000 restaurants in more than 150 countries. Nearly all are run by franchisees, so Yum earns mainly royalty fees. It was spun off from PepsiCo in 1997.

UGI.name: UGI Corporation
UGI.about: UGI owns AmeriGas, the largest U.S. propane distributor, a European propane business, natural gas pipelines and storage, and gas and electric utilities in Pennsylvania. Its roots go back to 1882 as United Gas Improvement.

PRU.name: Prudential Financial
PRU.about: Prudential is a major U.S. life insurer and retirement provider with a big business in Japan, and it owns PGIM, a large global asset manager. It sells life insurance, annuities, group benefits and pension risk transfers.

WEC.name: WEC Energy Group
WEC.about: WEC Energy runs electric and natural gas utilities serving about 4.7 million customers in Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan and Minnesota, including We Energies and Peoples Gas in Chicago, and owns a stake in the American Transmission Company. It was formerly Wisconsin Energy.

SWK.name: Stanley Black & Decker
SWK.about: Stanley Black & Decker is the world's largest tool maker — DeWalt, Craftsman, Stanley and Black+Decker power and hand tools — plus engineered fasteners for cars and aircraft. It has been cutting costs and debt after a sales slump.

PAG.name: Penske Automotive Group
PAG.about: Penske Automotive runs over 300 car dealerships in the U.S., U.K. and other countries, heavy on premium brands like BMW, Mercedes and Porsche, plus commercial truck dealerships and a stake in Penske Truck Leasing. Service and parts bring steady profit.

PEBO.name: Peoples Bancorp
PEBO.about: Peoples Bancorp is a community bank with about 120 branches in Ohio, West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia, Maryland and D.C., offering loans and deposits plus insurance, equipment leasing and trust services.

ADM.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland
ADM.about: ADM is one of the world's largest crop traders and processors: it buys, stores and ships grains and oilseeds and turns them into vegetable oils, animal feed, sweeteners, ethanol, flavors and nutrition ingredients. Its profits swing with crop margins and biofuel policy.

NWN.name: Northwest Natural Holding
NWN.about: Northwest Natural delivers natural gas to about 800,000 meters in Oregon and southwest Washington, owns the Mist gas storage field, and is building a small water utility business in the Northwest and Texas.

BBY.name: Best Buy
BBY.about: Best Buy is the largest U.S. consumer electronics store chain, with about 1,000 stores and a big website selling computers, phones, TVs, appliances and gaming, plus Geek Squad installation and repair services. Sales rise and fall with product upgrade cycles.

CWEN.name: Clearway Energy
CWEN.about: Clearway owns wind, solar and battery projects plus natural gas plants in the U.S., selling most of their power to utilities under long-term contracts and paying out most of its cash flow. It was formerly NRG Yield.

USB.name: U.S. Bancorp
USB.about: U.S. Bancorp is the fifth-largest U.S. bank, strongest in the Midwest and West, with a large payments business — corporate cards, merchant processing — and a big corporate trust and fund services arm.

TJX.name: TJX Companies
TJX.about: TJX runs T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods and Sierra in the U.S., Winners in Canada and T.K. Maxx in Europe and Australia — nearly 5,000 off-price stores selling brand-name clothing and home goods below department-store prices.

ARES.name: Ares Management
ARES.about: Ares is a large alternative asset manager best known for private credit — direct loans to mid-sized companies — plus real estate, private equity and infrastructure funds. It earns management and performance fees and pays out most of its earnings.

CSWC.name: Capital Southwest
CSWC.about: Capital Southwest is a business development company that lends to smaller private U.S. companies, mostly first-lien loans with small equity stakes alongside. It must pay out most of its income and also pays supplemental dividends.

APD.name: Air Products and Chemicals
APD.about: Air Products supplies industrial gases — oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, helium — to refineries, chemical plants, steelmakers, electronics and healthcare, often from on-site plants under 15- to 20-year contracts. It has been scaling back a costly push into clean hydrogen.

SR.name: Spire
SR.about: Spire delivers natural gas to about 1.7 million homes and businesses in Missouri, Alabama and Mississippi, and owns gas pipelines and storage. It was formerly The Laclede Group.

MAIN.name: Main Street Capital
MAIN.about: Main Street Capital is a business development company that lends to and takes equity stakes in small and mid-sized private U.S. companies. It pays a monthly dividend plus periodic supplemental dividends, and is run internally, which keeps its costs low.

DRI.name: Darden Restaurants
DRI.about: Darden is the largest U.S. full-service restaurant company, running about 2,100 restaurants including Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Cheddar's, Yard House, The Capital Grille and Ruth's Chris. It owns nearly all its locations rather than franchising.

TGT.name: Target
TGT.about: Target runs nearly 2,000 big-box stores across the U.S. selling groceries, household essentials, clothing, home goods and electronics, with a large share of sales from its own store brands. It has struggled with slower sales in discretionary goods.

HRB.name: H&R Block
HRB.about: H&R Block prepares income tax returns in person at about 9,000 offices and through do-it-yourself software in the U.S., Canada and Australia, and offers small-business bookkeeping through Wave. Nearly all its revenue comes in the first four months of the year.

ENB.name: Enbridge
ENB.about: Enbridge runs the world's longest crude oil pipeline system, carrying much of Canada's oil exports to the U.S., plus major gas pipelines and North America's largest gas utility by volume. Most of its earnings come from regulated or contracted fees.

SHW.name: Sherwin-Williams
SHW.about: Sherwin-Williams is the largest U.S. paint and coatings company, selling mainly to professional painters through over 4,000 of its own stores, plus Valspar and other brands at home centers and industrial coatings worldwide.

ICE.name: Intercontinental Exchange
ICE.about: ICE owns the New York Stock Exchange, major energy and commodity futures exchanges and clearing houses, a large bond-data and index business, and mortgage software (Encompass, Black Knight). Much of its revenue is recurring data and software fees.

BANF.name: BancFirst
BANF.about: BancFirst is Oklahoma's largest state-chartered bank, with over 100 branches across Oklahoma plus offices in Texas, serving consumers, small businesses and energy and agriculture borrowers. The Rainbolt family holds a large stake.

PG.name: Procter & Gamble
PG.about: Procter & Gamble is the world's largest consumer products company: Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Crest, Charmin, Bounty, Dawn, Head & Shoulders, Olay and Oral-B. It sells in over 180 countries and has raised its dividend every year for more than 65 years.

WLY.name: John Wiley & Sons
WLY.about: Wiley publishes scientific and medical research journals and professional and educational books, and increasingly licenses its content to AI companies. The founding Wiley family still controls it through a separate share class.

MO.name: Altria Group
MO.about: Altria sells Marlboro, the top U.S. cigarette brand, plus Black & Mild cigars, Copenhagen and Skoal smokeless tobacco and on! nicotine pouches. U.S. cigarette volumes keep shrinking, offset by price increases. It pays out most of its earnings as dividends.

MPLX.name: MPLX
MPLX.about: MPLX owns pipelines, storage terminals and gas processing plants, largely serving its parent Marathon Petroleum's refineries plus Permian and Appalachian gas producers. It earns mostly fee-based income. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

FCBC.name: First Community Bankshares
FCBC.about: First Community is a community bank with about 50 branches in southern West Virginia, Virginia, North Carolina and Tennessee, offering consumer and business loans, deposits and wealth management.

NTR.name: Nutrien
NTR.about: Nutrien is the world's largest potash producer and a major maker of nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers, and runs about 2,000 farm retail stores selling seed, crop protection and fertilizer to growers. It was formed from the 2018 merger of PotashCorp and Agrium.

BEN.name: Franklin Resources
BEN.about: Franklin Templeton manages stock, bond and alternative funds for individuals and institutions, and grew through deals like Legg Mason, Western Asset, Putnam and Clarion Partners. Its fee income moves with markets and fund flows. The Johnson family remains a large holder.

BTI.name: British American Tobacco
BTI.about: British American Tobacco is the world's second-largest tobacco company — Newport, Camel, Lucky Strike, Dunhill and Pall Mall cigarettes — and is building a smokeless business with Vuse vapes, glo heated tobacco and Velo pouches. It trades in the U.S. as an ADR.

ET.name: Energy Transfer
ET.about: Energy Transfer runs one of the largest U.S. pipeline networks — over 130,000 miles moving natural gas, natural gas liquids, crude oil and refined products — plus export terminals and fractionation plants. It also owns stakes in Sunoco and USA Compression. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

OKE.name: ONEOK
OKE.about: ONEOK gathers, processes and transports natural gas and natural gas liquids from the Rockies, Mid-Continent and Permian to Gulf Coast markets, and has grown through deals for Magellan, EnLink and Medallion. Most of its income is fee-based.

CNS.name: Cohen & Steers
CNS.about: Cohen & Steers is an asset manager specializing in real assets — REITs, listed infrastructure, preferred securities and natural resources — for mutual funds, closed-end funds and institutions. Its fees move with real estate and income-stock markets.

NFG.name: National Fuel Gas
NFG.about: National Fuel Gas produces natural gas in Appalachia through Seneca Resources, runs gathering lines and interstate pipelines and storage, and owns the gas utility serving about 750,000 customers in western New York and Pennsylvania.

HASI.name: HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital
HASI.about: HASI (formerly Hannon Armstrong) invests in and lends to clean energy projects — solar, wind, energy efficiency and renewable natural gas — usually holding senior or preferred positions in long-term contracted assets.

WM.name: Waste Management
WM.about: WM is North America's largest trash and recycling company, owning about 260 landfills — the hardest assets to replicate — plus collection routes, transfer stations and recycling plants. It added a medical waste business with the Stericycle purchase.

DKL.name: Delek Logistics Partners
DKL.about: Delek Logistics owns pipelines, terminals and storage serving Delek US's refineries in Texas and Arkansas, plus Permian gathering and processing assets. Delek US is its main customer and controls it. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

FNLC.name: The First Bancorp
FNLC.about: The First Bancorp owns First National Bank, a community bank with 18 branches along Maine's mid-coast and Down East regions, offering loans, deposits, trust and wealth management.

KMI.name: Kinder Morgan
KMI.about: Kinder Morgan operates about 79,000 miles of pipelines — the largest natural gas transmission network in the U.S. — plus refined-products pipelines, storage terminals and CO2 operations. Nearly all its cash flow comes from fees and contracts.

QCOM.name: Qualcomm
QCOM.about: Qualcomm designs the Snapdragon processors and modems in most Android phones and collects royalties on nearly every 3G, 4G and 5G phone sold. It is expanding into chips for cars, PCs and AI devices as Apple moves to its own modems.

EPD.name: Enterprise Products Partners
EPD.about: Enterprise Products is one of the largest U.S. pipeline partnerships, with about 50,000 miles of pipelines for natural gas liquids, crude, natural gas and petrochemicals, plus Gulf Coast fractionators and export docks. It has raised its distribution every year since its 1998 IPO. It is a partnership that issues K-1 tax forms.

AFG.name: American Financial Group
AFG.about: American Financial Group (Great American Insurance) writes specialty commercial insurance — crop, trucking, marine, executive liability, workers' comp and surety — sold through independent agents. It regularly pays large special dividends on top of its regular one. The Lindner family leads it.

MSFT.name: Microsoft
MSFT.about: Microsoft sells Windows, Office 365, Teams and LinkedIn, and runs Azure, the second-largest cloud computing platform, which is now its main growth engine thanks to AI demand. It also owns Xbox and Activision Blizzard and is a major investor in OpenAI.

GD.name: General Dynamics
GD.about: General Dynamics builds Gulfstream business jets, U.S. Navy nuclear submarines (with Electric Boat) and destroyers, Abrams tanks and Stryker vehicles, and provides IT services to defense and intelligence agencies. Most revenue comes from the U.S. government.

IVZ.name: Invesco
IVZ.about: Invesco manages mutual funds and ETFs — including the QQQ Nasdaq-100 ETF — plus bond, real estate and alternative funds for individuals and institutions worldwide. Its fees move with markets and fund flows. It is legally domiciled in Bermuda.

BKH.name: Black Hills
BKH.about: Black Hills supplies natural gas to about 1.1 million customers and electricity to about 220,000 across eight Midwest and Mountain West states, from Arkansas to Wyoming. It agreed in 2025 to merge with NorthWestern Energy.

CL.name: Colgate-Palmolive
CL.about: Colgate is the world's top toothpaste brand and also sells Palmolive, Softsoap, Irish Spring, Speed Stick and Fabuloso, plus Hill's pet food. About 70% of its sales come from outside the U.S., including many emerging markets.

ROST.name: Ross Stores
ROST.about: Ross runs about 2,200 Ross Dress for Less and dd's DISCOUNTS stores selling brand-name clothing, shoes and home goods at 20–70% below department-store prices, mainly to middle- and lower-income shoppers.

AMP.name: Ameriprise Financial
AMP.about: Ameriprise runs a network of about 10,000 financial advisors, manages funds through Columbia Threadneedle, and sells annuities and life insurance through RiverSource. It was spun off from American Express in 2005 and buys back a lot of stock.

JPM.name: JPMorgan Chase
JPM.about: JPMorgan Chase is the largest U.S. bank: Chase consumer banking and credit cards, the top-ranked investment bank and trading business, commercial banking, and J.P. Morgan asset and wealth management. It is widely seen as the strongest-run large bank.

XOM.name: Exxon Mobil
XOM.about: Exxon Mobil is the largest U.S. oil company, producing oil and gas worldwide — with growth from the Permian Basin (boosted by its Pioneer purchase) and Guyana — and running refineries and chemical plants. Its profits move with oil and gas prices.

COST.name: Costco
COST.about: Costco runs about 900 membership warehouse stores worldwide selling groceries, household goods, electronics and gas in bulk at thin margins. Membership fees bring in most of its profit, and it pays occasional large special dividends.

CVX.name: Chevron
CVX.about: Chevron is the second-largest U.S. oil company, producing oil and gas in the Permian, Gulf of Mexico, Kazakhstan, Australia and, since buying Hess, Guyana, and running refineries and fuel stations. It has raised its dividend for over 35 straight years.

AFL.name: Aflac
AFL.about: Aflac sells supplemental health insurance — cancer, accident, hospital and disability policies that pay cash benefits — in Japan, its largest market, and in the U.S. through payroll deduction at employers. It has raised its dividend for over 40 years.

PFG.name: Principal Financial Group
PFG.about: Principal is a leading provider of 401(k) plans for small and mid-sized businesses, manages money through Principal Asset Management, and sells life and disability insurance. It went public in 2001 after converting from a mutual insurer.

ALL.name: Allstate
ALL.about: Allstate is one of the largest U.S. home and car insurers, selling through its own agents and online, plus the National General brand for independent agents. Results swing with catastrophe losses and repair costs. It was spun off from Sears in 1995.

LLY.name: Eli Lilly
LLY.about: Eli Lilly is the world's most valuable drugmaker thanks to its diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, plus cancer, immunology and Alzheimer's treatments. Its dividend yield is low because its share price has risen so far.

ETN.name: Eaton
ETN.about: Eaton makes electrical equipment — switchgear, circuit breakers, transformers and backup power — used in data centers, utilities, buildings and factories, plus aerospace fuel and hydraulic systems and vehicle drivetrains. Data-center demand is its biggest growth driver.

LMT.name: Lockheed Martin
LMT.about: Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defense contractor: the F-35 fighter, missiles and missile defense (PAC-3, THAAD), Sikorsky helicopters, and satellites and space systems. About 70% of sales go to the U.S. government.

ORI.name: Old Republic International
ORI.about: Old Republic writes specialty commercial insurance — trucking, workers' comp, construction and financial lines — and is one of the largest U.S. title insurers. It often pays special dividends and has raised its regular dividend for over 40 years.

AVGO.name: Broadcom
AVGO.about: Broadcom designs networking, wireless and custom AI chips used in data centers and smartphones, and owns a large infrastructure software business built from VMware, CA and Symantec. Custom AI accelerators for big tech companies are its fastest-growing line.

IBM.name: IBM
IBM.about: IBM sells hybrid-cloud and AI software (including Red Hat), IT consulting, and mainframe computers that still run much of the world's banking and airline systems. Software is now its largest and most profitable segment.

OGE.name: OGE Energy
OGE.about: OGE Energy owns Oklahoma Gas and Electric, which supplies power to about 900,000 customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas from gas, coal, wind and solar plants. State regulators set its rates.

UBSI.name: United Bankshares
UBSI.about: United Bankshares runs about 240 branches from West Virginia through the Washington, D.C. area, Virginia and the Carolinas to Georgia, offering commercial and consumer banking and mortgages. It has raised its dividend for over 50 straight years.

AMGN.name: Amgen
AMGN.about: Amgen is one of the largest biotech companies, selling drugs for bone loss (Prolia), cholesterol (Repatha), psoriasis (Otezla), cancer and rare diseases, and is developing an obesity drug, MariTide. Older drugs face competition from biosimilars.

CINF.name: Cincinnati Financial
CINF.about: Cincinnati Financial sells commercial and personal property-casualty insurance through independent agents, mostly in the Midwest and South, and holds a large stock portfolio alongside its bonds. It has raised its dividend for over 60 straight years.

NWE.name: NorthWestern Energy Group
NWE.about: NorthWestern Energy supplies electricity and natural gas to about 775,000 customers in Montana, South Dakota and Nebraska, including Yellowstone National Park. It agreed in 2025 to merge with Black Hills.

SO.name: Southern Company
SO.about: Southern Company owns Georgia Power, Alabama Power and Mississippi Power plus gas utilities in four states, serving about 9 million customers. It finished the Vogtle nuclear expansion in 2024 and is adding capacity for data centers in Georgia.

WMT.name: Walmart
WMT.about: Walmart is the world's largest retailer, with about 10,500 stores and Sam's Club warehouses, a fast-growing online and advertising business, and stakes in Flipkart (India) and Walmex (Mexico). Groceries are over half its U.S. sales. It moved its listing to the Nasdaq in 2025.

R.name: Ryder System
R.about: Ryder leases, rents and maintains commercial trucks for businesses, runs warehouses and supply-chain operations, and provides dedicated trucks with drivers. Used-truck sales and rental demand make its earnings cyclical.

RLI.name: RLI Corp.
RLI.about: RLI is a specialty insurer covering niche commercial risks — general and professional liability, trucking, marine, surety bonds and some homeowners in Hawaii — known for decades of underwriting profits. It pays a special dividend most years on top of its regular one.

CAT.name: Caterpillar
CAT.about: Caterpillar is the world's largest maker of construction and mining equipment, diesel and gas engines, industrial turbines and locomotives. Engines and turbines for data-center power have become a big growth area. Its sales follow the construction and mining cycle.

PM.name: Philip Morris International
PM.about: Philip Morris International sells Marlboro and other cigarettes everywhere except the U.S., and leads in smoke-free products — IQOS heated tobacco and ZYN nicotine pouches, which now make up over a third of its revenue. It was spun off from Altria in 2008.

TXN.name: Texas Instruments
TXN.about: Texas Instruments makes analog and embedded chips — power management, sensors and microcontrollers — used in cars, factories and electronics of all kinds, sold to over 100,000 customers. It is investing heavily in new U.S. chip plants.

ABBV.name: AbbVie
ABBV.about: AbbVie is a large drugmaker whose immunology drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq have replaced Humira as its growth engines, plus cancer, neuroscience and Botox aesthetics. It was spun off from Abbott Laboratories in 2013 and counts Abbott's dividend history as its own.

FAST.name: Fastenal
FAST.about: Fastenal distributes fasteners, tools and safety supplies to manufacturers and contractors, increasingly through vending machines and on-site stores inside customers' plants. It carries very little debt.

VLO.name: Valero Energy
VLO.about: Valero is the largest independent U.S. oil refiner, with about 15 refineries in the U.S., Canada and the U.K., plus ethanol plants and a stake in the largest U.S. renewable diesel producer. Its profits swing with refining margins.

EMR.name: Emerson Electric
EMR.about: Emerson makes automation equipment — control systems, valves, measurement instruments and industrial software (it now fully owns AspenTech) — for energy, chemical, pharmaceutical and factory customers. It has sold off its consumer and climate businesses to focus on automation.

GILD.name: Gilead Sciences
GILD.about: Gilead is the leading maker of HIV drugs, led by Biktarvy and the new twice-yearly prevention shot Yeztugo, plus liver disease and cancer treatments. HIV medicines bring in most of its revenue.

PSX.name: Phillips 66
PSX.about: Phillips 66 runs oil refineries in the U.S. and Europe, a large pipeline and natural gas liquids business, a chemicals joint venture (CPChem) and Phillips 66, 76 and Conoco fuel stations. It was spun off from ConocoPhillips in 2012.

MRK.name: Merck & Co.
MRK.about: Merck sells Keytruda, the world's top-selling cancer drug, plus Gardasil HPV vaccine, other vaccines and an animal health business. Keytruda's main patent expires in 2028, which is the key question for investors.

CAH.name: Cardinal Health
CAH.about: Cardinal Health is one of the three big U.S. drug wholesalers, delivering prescription medicines to pharmacies and hospitals, and also makes and distributes medical and surgical supplies. It earns thin margins on very large volumes.

ED.name: Consolidated Edison
ED.about: Con Edison delivers electricity to about 3.7 million customers in New York City and Westchester, natural gas to over a million, and runs the Manhattan steam system. It has raised its dividend for over 50 straight years.

DUK.name: Duke Energy
DUK.about: Duke Energy is one of the largest U.S. utilities, supplying electricity to about 8.6 million customers in the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky and natural gas to 1.7 million. It is investing heavily in new generation and grid upgrades.

CME.name: CME Group
CME.about: CME Group runs the world's largest futures exchange, where interest rate, stock index, oil, gas, metals and crop futures are traded and cleared. It pays a regular dividend plus a large annual variable dividend each year.

TRV.name: Travelers
TRV.about: Travelers is one of the largest U.S. commercial and personal insurers, covering businesses, homes and cars through independent agents, plus surety bonds and management liability. Results swing with storm and catastrophe losses.

RTX.name: RTX
RTX.about: RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies) makes Pratt & Whitney jet engines, Collins Aerospace aircraft systems, and Raytheon missiles and defense systems such as the Patriot. Commercial aftermarket parts and service are a big profit source.

JNJ.name: Johnson & Johnson
JNJ.about: Johnson & Johnson is the largest U.S. healthcare company, with prescription drugs in cancer, immunology and neuroscience, plus surgical, orthopedic, heart and vision devices. It spun off its consumer brands as Kenvue in 2023 and has raised its dividend for over 60 years.

CSCO.name: Cisco Systems
CSCO.about: Cisco is the leading maker of networking gear — routers, switches, Wi-Fi — plus security software and, since buying Splunk, data-monitoring software. A growing share of revenue is subscriptions, and AI data-center networking is a new growth area.

KO.name: Coca-Cola
KO.about: Coca-Cola sells drink concentrates and brands — Coke, Sprite, Fanta, Dasani, Powerade, Minute Maid, fairlife — in over 200 countries, mostly through independent bottlers. It has raised its dividend for over 60 straight years.

UNM.name: Unum Group
UNM.about: Unum is the largest U.S. provider of workplace disability insurance and also sells group life, dental, vision and supplemental policies through employers (Colonial Life), with operations in the U.K. and Poland.

WRB.name: W. R. Berkley
WRB.about: W. R. Berkley runs about 60 specialty commercial insurance and reinsurance units covering niche risks — professional liability, workers' comp, excess and surplus lines. It pays special dividends most years. The Berkley family leads it, and Mitsui Sumitomo is building a large stake.

WTRG.name: Essential Utilities
WTRG.about: Essential Utilities runs Aqua water and wastewater systems in eight states and Peoples natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and West Virginia, serving about 5.5 million people. It was formerly Aqua America.
